rationale: The puzzle benchmark is a tiny, compute-bound BenchmarkGame program with no available static profile (zero lines, unknown function count), so the safest strategy is to rely on passes whose costs are small and bounded regardless of program shape: SUB is cheap, universally applicable arithmetic transformation with solid diversity, so it gets the strongest weights; FLA and BCF give the best reverse-engineering resistance on control-flow-heavy hot loops, but their runtime/size costs are kept moderate (0.3-0.4) since a tight benchmark loop amplifies dispatch and bogus-path overhead; SPLIT is low-risk structural diversity with negligible cost, weighted as a cheap complement; IBR and ICALL are included at lower weights because a benchmark of this kind has few indirectible branches or call sites, so their high per-use overhead is unlikely to pay off and their correctness risk (indirect target resolution) warrants restraint; IGV sits in the middle as a low-risk global-variable transformation that adds diversity without interacting with the hot loop. All passes are retained with risk weights capped at 0.3 to bias the selector away from aggressive application on unprofiled code while still allowing feature-driven selection where the five dimensions favor it.
